message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint in Atlanta, but it’s usually handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** or the **Code Enforcement Division**, not directly by the city council. The council can refer you to the right department and can take action if the issue is widespread or involves a city‑owned property. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Identify the source** | Is it a residential neighbor, a business, a construction site, or a city‑owned facility? | This will determine which department is responsible. | | **2. Gather details** | Date, time, location, description of the noise, how long it lasts, any witnesses, and photos/video if possible. | Keep a written log. | | **3. Contact the appropriate agency** | • **Atlanta Police Department (APD)** – for immediate disturbances or if you’re in danger.
• **Code Enforcement Division** – for ongoing or repeated violations of the city’s noise ordinance.
• **Atlanta 311** – for general inquiries and to be directed to the right department. | • APD: 404‑656‑3111 (non‑emergency) or 911 if it’s an emergency.
• Code Enforcement: 404‑656‑3111 (same line as 311).
• 311: 404‑656‑3111 or online at . | | **4. File online (if available)** | The City of Atlanta offers an online portal for many service requests, including noise complaints. | Visit and select “Noise Complaint” under “Service Requests.” | | **5. Follow up** | If you don’t hear back within a few days, call 311 or the department you contacted. | Keep your complaint reference number handy. | | **6. Escalate if necessary** | If the issue persists, you can bring it to the attention of your local city council member or the City Council’s public safety committee. | Email or call the office of your council member (contact info on the city website). | --- ## Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Key Points) | Time | Allowed Noise Level | Typical Violations | |------|---------------------|--------------------| | **Weekdays** | 7 a.m. – 10 p.m. | Construction, loud music, barking dogs, etc. | | **Weekends & Holidays** | 8 a.m. – 11 p.m. | Same as weekdays, but with slightly later start. | | **Quiet Hours** | 10 p.m. – 7 a.m. | No loud music, no construction, no barking dogs, no loud parties. | *Violations can result in fines, citations, or even civil penalties if the noise is persistent.* --- ## Who Handles Noise Complaints? | Agency | Role | |--------|------| | **Atlanta Police Department** | Responds to immediate disturbances, enforces the noise ordinance, and can issue citations. | | **Code Enforcement Division** | Handles repeat or ongoing violations, conducts inspections, and can impose fines. | | **City Council** | Sets policy, can hold hearings on widespread issues, and can direct resources to address systemic problems. | --- ## Quick Contact List | Agency | Phone | Website | |--------|-------|---------| | **Atlanta Police Department (Non‑Emergency)** | 404‑656‑3111 | | | **Atlanta 311 (General Inquiries)** | 404‑656‑3111 | | | **City of Atlanta – Code Enforcement** | 404‑656‑3111 | | | **City Council – Public Safety Committee** | 404‑656‑3111 | | --- ### Bottom Line - **Yes, you can report a noise complaint in Atlanta.** - Use **311** or the **APD** for immediate concerns. - For ongoing issues, file with **Code Enforcement** (online or by phone). - The **city council** can help if the problem is widespread or involves city property. If you need more specific guidance—such as how to file a formal complaint with the council or how to appeal a citation—feel free to ask!
